hens_rule_text: Up to 8 hens and/or ducks combined are allowed on a residential lot with a Food-Producing Animal permit.
permit_notes: A one-time Food-Producing Animal permit, reported at a $25 fee, is obtained through Denver Animal Protection before keeping hens.
setback_notes: Coop must be at least 15 ft from any neighboring residence; separate zoning or accessory-structure review can also apply to the coop itself.
coop_rules: Coop must be a covered, predator-resistant enclosure kept clean and sanitary.
zoning_notes: Rules are administered under Denver Municipal Code Ch. 8 (Animals), reported around Sec. 8-91, separately from any zoning or building review of the coop structure.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: American Farmland Trust, Denver Colorado Urban Livestock Ordinance
CoopCraft Guide, Denver Colorado Chicken Laws

research_notes: Denver's municipal code was not opened directly (Municode region block, no Wayback copy found); the 8-bird cap, $25 permit fee and 15 ft setback all come from secondary summaries, not the code text or an official city permit page.
